Empirical Research Plan ‑ Chilean Trade Liberalisation and Plant-level Productivity, 1979-1986
==================================================================

------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------------
Difference-in-Differences (DID) with industry*year variation (two-way fixed effects).

Why it fits  
•  We have a panel of plants observed before and after most adjustment to a nationwide, **uniform** tariff cut.  
•  Because all industries faced the same statutory tariffs, *cross-industry heterogeneity in the
intensity of foreign competition is driven by pre-existing import and export exposure*, not by policy endogeneity.  
•  Comparing high-exposure (import-competing or export-oriented) industries to non-traded industries over time gives a credible counterfactual trend for what would have happened absent foreign competition.  
•  Within-plant fixed effects purge time-invariant unobservables; year fixed effects absorb macro shocks (e.g. 1982 crisis).  

The DID is augmented with continuous exposure measures (initial import-penetration and export-share) to increase power and allow decomposing effects by exposure intensity (a Bartik-type design).

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control Definition
------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
    TradeExposure_ic = ImportPenetration1980_c  for import-competing industries  
                   or  ExportShare1980_c        for export-oriented industries  
    (continuous 0–1; set to 0 for non-traded).

Binary versions used for graphical diagnostics:  
    Treated_i = 1 if ImportPenetration1980_c ≥ 0.15  OR ExportShare1980_c ≥ 0.15  
    Control_i = 0 otherwise.

Control group  
Plants in “non-traded” four-digit ISIC sectors (imports+exports ≤ 15 % of dom. output).

Treatment timing  
t = 1979…1986. We regard 1979 as the *baseline post-liberalisation* year. The DID coefficient therefore captures *differential* post-liberalisation adjustment paths rather than the immediate impact of the tariff cut itself.

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: Absent foreign-competition exposure, productivity in high- and low-exposure industries would have followed the same trend 1979-86.  
 Plausibility: uniform macro environment, similar factor market policies; we will test in 1979-81 pre-trend window and with placebo outcomes (e.g. electricity expenditure).

A2. Exogeneity of initial exposure: 1980 import-penetration/export-share are predetermined with respect to post-79 productivity shocks at the plant level.  
 Plausibility: exposure measured at industry level; unlikely that individual-plant productivity shocks feed back into national trade flows.

A3. No spillovers that differentially affect the control group (SUTVA): Productivity improvements in treated industries do not systematically raise or lower productivity in non-traded industries.  
 Plausibility: some general-equilibrium effects may exist (e.g. input markets) but uniform tariffs and limited vertical links in small open Chilean economy mitigate concerns.

------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigations
------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential industry-specific shocks unrelated to trade (e.g. technology, demand).  
 Mitigation: include industry*global commodity-price controls; interact world price indices with input shares; add industry-specific capital good price indices.

T2. Composition bias from entry/exit (reallocation channel conflates with within-plant).  
 Mitigation: (i) estimate specifications on balanced (“stayers”) sample for within-plant effect; (ii) use Olley-Pakes decomposition to separate within vs. between components.

T3. Measurement error in import penetration & export share.  
 Mitigation: instrument continuous TradeExposure with world-export-supply shocks as in Autor-Dorn-Hanson style Bartik:  
  Z_ct = Σ_k (WorldExportGrowth_kt × 1980ChileImportShare_ck).

------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# Load packages ----------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # TWFE regressions
library(readr)        # csv
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data -----------------------------------------------------
plant  <- fread("chile_plants_1979_1986.csv")   # main CES data
trade  <- fread("industry_trade_1980.csv")      # import pen., export share 1980
price  <- fread("world_prices_1979_1986.csv")   # for controls (optional)

# 2. Merge & construct variables ----------------------------------
dt <- merge(plant, trade, by = "isic4", all.x = TRUE)

# Plant-level TFP via simple Solow residual (placeholder) ----------
# lnTFP = ln(output) - alpha*ln(capital) - beta*ln(labor) - gamma*ln(materials)
# Using industry-avg factor shares:
dt[, ln_output  := log(gross_output)]
dt[, ln_capital := log(capital_stock)]
dt[, ln_labor   := log(skilled + unskilled)]
dt[, ln_material:= log(intermediate_materials)]

# assume 0.3 K, 0.6 L, 0.1 M (replace with industry shares)
dt[, lnTFP := ln_output - 0.3*ln_capital - 0.6*ln_labor - 0.1*ln_material]

# Treatment variables ---------------------------------------------
dt[, treat_bin := (import_penetration1980 >= .15 | export_share1980 >= .15)]
dt[, trade_exposure := import_penetration1980 + export_share1980]   # 0 for non-traded

# 3. Main DID specification ---------------------------------------
did_eq <- feols(lnTFP ~ trade_exposure:year + ## event-time effects
                          capital_lag + labor_lag | plant_id + year,
                data = dt, cluster = ~isic4)

# 4. Within-plant vs. reallocation decomposition ------------------
# Olley-Pakes: within + covariance
# Step 1: industry-year mean TFP
op <- dt[, .(mean_tfp = weighted.mean(lnTFP, gross_output, na.rm=TRUE)),
          by = .(isic4, year)]
# Step 2: covariance
# (details skipped)

# 5. Robustness: balanced sample of stayers -----------------------
stayers <- dt[, .N, by = plant_id][N==8]$plant_id  # present all years
dt_bal  <- dt[plant_id %in% stayers]

did_bal <- feols(lnTFP ~ trade_exposure:year | plant_id + year,
                 data = dt_bal, cluster=~isic4)

# 6. Pre-trend test -----------------------------------------------
pre   <- dt[year <= 1981]
pre_did <- feols(lnTFP ~ trade_exposure:year | plant_id + year,
                 data = pre, cluster=~isic4)
summary(pre_did)

# 7. Plot event-study coefficients --------------------------------
coefplot(did_eq, keep="trade_exposure")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory (Melitz, 2003): tougher foreign competition raises aggregate productivity mainly through *selection* (exit of low-productivity plants) and *reallocation* (market-share gains by efficient plants). Within-plant upgrading also occurs but is smaller.

Prediction  
•  Average TFP in high-exposure industries grows ≈ 2–3 p.p. per year faster than in non-traded industries, cumulating to ~15 % by 1986.  
•  Decomposition: ≥ 60 % of the gain from reallocation (exit & market-share shifts), ≤ 40 % from within-plant improvements.

------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
------------------------------------------------------------------
C1. No omitted shocks correlated with exposure (parallel trends): 0.7  
C2. Treatment exogeneity to plant-level outcomes: 0.8  
C3. No anticipation / reverse causality: 0.8  
C4. Stable composition of treatment & control groups: 0.6  
C5. No spillovers or interference: 0.7  
Total (out of 5) = 3.6 → reasonably credible but not bullet-proof.

------------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
